title: Version 1.0
body:
# Version 1.0

This pull request is a placeholder for triaging a 1.0 release against.

Version 1.0 is not planned to introduce breaking changes. We are updating our supported Python versions, and may be updating our SSL defaults and re-reviewing other security-related changes as part of the release.

## Why the delay?

Issues and pull requests on the httpx repository had [previously been closed](#3784). GitHub have since introduced access controls allowing us to ensure visibility, while limiting access to project maintainers. 

We have also been quietly working towards a more comprehensive redesign, which we'll be sharing details of in due course.

title: Bump cryptography from 45.0.7 to 46.0.6
body:
Bumps [cryptography](https://github.com/pyca/cryptography) from 45.0.7 to 46.0.6.
Changelog

Sourced from cryptography's changelog.

46.0.6 - 2026-03-25


* **SECURITY ISSUE**: Fixed a bug where name constraints were not applied
  to peer names during verification when the leaf certificate contains a
  wildcard DNS SAN. Ordinary X.509 topologies are not affected by this bug,
  including those used by the Web PKI. Credit to **Oleh Konko (1seal)** for
  reporting the issue. **CVE-2026-34073**

.. _v46-0-5:


46.0.5 - 2026-02-10

  • An attacker could create a malicious public key that reveals portions of your private key when using certain uncommon elliptic curves (binary curves). This version now includes additional security checks to prevent this attack. This issue only affects binary elliptic curves, which are rarely used in real-world applications. Credit to XlabAI Team of Tencent Xuanwu Lab and Atuin Automated Vulnerability Discovery Engine for reporting the issue. CVE-2026-26007
  • Support for SECT* binary elliptic curves is deprecated and will be removed in the next release.

.. v46-0-4:

46.0.4 - 2026-01-27


* `Dropped support for win_arm64 wheels`_.
* Updated Windows, macOS, and Linux wheels to be compiled with OpenSSL 3.5.5.

.. _v46-0-3:


46.0.3 - 2025-10-15

  • Fixed compilation when using LibreSSL 4.2.0.

.. _v46-0-2:

46.0.2 - 2025-09-30


* Updated Windows, macOS, and Linux wheels to be compiled with OpenSSL 3.5.4.

title: Add option to keep the same method for 301/302 redirects
body:
# Summary

RFC hasn't been clear enough about the expected behavior for 301 and 302 response. While it's (unfortunately) common for browsers to switch the original http method to GET when following redirects, some server applications expects the "legacy" behavior which keeps the same method over redirects.

Add new option to clients to select the behavior.

# Checklist

- [x] I understand that this PR may be closed in case there was no previous discussion. (This doesn't apply to typos!)
- [x] I've added a test for each change that was introduced, and I tried as much as possible to make a single atomic change.
- [x] I've updated the documentation accordingly.
